comparator.name: Biomedical Sciences (Biomedische Wetenschappen)
comparator.academicYear: Adopted Biomedical Sciences OER 2026–27, articles 11–12 and current 2026–27 study guide; checked 2026-09-26
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–27 OER lists nine compulsory 6-EC year-one components plus one 6-EC restricted choice, nine compulsory 6-EC year-two components plus a separate 6-EC restricted choice, and year three with 30 EC genuinely open minor space, one 6-EC restricted choice and one of two mutually exclusive 24-EC thesis formats. The first-listed option in the formally adopted OER is instantiated at each choice point: Biomedical Sciences and Society, Pathophysiology of Heart and Circulation, Epidemiology, and the Experimental thesis. The study-guide display order differs from OER in the year-one and year-three choice lists; the OER order supplies the neutral choices. Zero-credit lab safety and language assessment are excluded. Optional minors and thesis formats are not formal named graduation routes. The general prospective page refers to the forthcoming 2027–28 intake, so the 2026–27 OER governs this comparator.

alternatives.concept: Combines molecular and cellular biology, anatomy and physiology, immunity, pharmacology, disease mechanisms and neuroscience with laboratory, statistical and ethical study. It reflects the compulsory VU core while UCR lacks dedicated oncology, omics and a 24-EC experimental thesis placement.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad biomedical route, population-health interventions, and quantitative biomedical analysis arise sequentially from distinct target-specific evidence. Each produces a coherent 24-course curriculum, passes workbook feasibility and changes at least five courses against every other route. The data direction explicitly preserves the gap in VU omics and the formal thesis.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both develop academic and professional direction, with UCR PPD covering a different and broader programme.
Both relate human anatomy to physiological function; UCR is organized by body regions and systems.
Both study pharmacological actions, effects and therapeutic use.
Both examine immune mechanisms and response to infection.
Both study cardiovascular pathophysiology; UCR covers multiple organ systems rather than only the heart and circulation.
Both teach biological neuroscience, with UCR not limited to human medical contexts.
Both introduce biomedical foundations from cells to body systems.
Both examine human cell structures and their function, although UCR is broader molecular cell biology.
Both study molecular biochemistry and metabolism.
Both address genetic mechanisms in human disease; UCR combines pathology and genetics.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Humane Ontwikkeling component; its 6 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Microbiologie component; its 6 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Humane Evolutie component; its 6 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Medical Biochemistry component; its 6 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Oncology component; its 6 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
Both address ethical reasoning; UCR ethics is broader than biomedical philosophy of science.
Both teach epidemiological study of disease risk and population-level evidence.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Biomedische Wetenschappen en de Maatschappij component; its 6 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Vrije keuzeruimte / minor component; its 30 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
Both teach statistical research design, though UCR is general and not biomedical-specific.
Both introduce empirical research and statistics; UCR emphasizes human experimental methods.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Omics component; its 6 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.
No selected UCR course directly reproduces the VU Bachelor Thesis Biomedical Sciences - Experimental component; its 24 EC and compulsory or choice status remain explicit.

notes.text: VU requires a prescribed molecular, anatomical and clinical sequence, three separately restricted 6-EC choices, and a 24-EC experimental or data-analysis research thesis alongside an open 30-EC minor. UCR can combine biomedical, public-health and data study but does not duplicate specialised oncology, omics, microbiology laboratory or the VU thesis placement.
